implemented_requirements.evidence: DIFFICULTIES dict in game.py defines (9,9,10), (16,16,40), (16,30,99) and gui.py populates an OptionMenu from this dict.
gui.py binds left mouse button (<Button-1>) to _uncover which calls Board.reveal.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.place_mines computes cell.adjacent; gui._refresh displays the number with appropriate color when cell.revealed and not a mine.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Losing when a mine is uncovered
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.reveal sets game_over=True and calls _reveal_all_mines when a mined cell is revealed; gui shows "Boom! Game Over" status.
After each reveal or flag, gui._refresh iterates over all cells and updates button text, background, and relief.
gui binds right and middle mouse buttons to _flag which calls Board.toggle_flag; flagged state stored in Cell.flagged.
gui._refresh configures flagged cells with FLAG_BG background and shows "🚩" (or "❌" on loss).

critical_issues: No explicit handling for environments without a display (headless); running the GUI in such an environment would raise an error.
The win‑condition auto‑flags remaining mines but does not update the mine counter label until the next refresh, which could momentarily show an incorrect count.
judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional classic Minesweeper game with three difficulty levels, cell uncovering, adjacency numbers, loss on mine, board refresh after each action, and a flagging system with distinct visuals. All core requirements are satisfied, and the code appears ready to run under a standard Python environment with Tkinter. Minor usability concerns exist but do not affect core functionality.
